Subject: Medix Health POC — success criteria & high-level timeline

Jordan / Asha — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we put the trial plan into a formal doc: 

Summary of what Medix wants to validate
- Accuracy: end-to-end extraction accuracy on three representative forms (intake, consent, billing) with F1 >= 0.88 on the gold set
- Latency: median API response < 300ms at sample QPS of 8
- Data handling: logs redacted, model outputs stored only in Medix test bucket for the duration of the trial

Proposed trial structure (2-week sandbox + 4-week pilot):
- Week 0: kick-off, sample ingestion and mapping
- Weeks 1–2: sandbox runs, baseline QC, measure accuracy on labelled subset
- Weeks 3–6: pilot with live traffic mirror, business metrics evaluation (time saved per document)

Immediate asks from your side
1) Confirm the three form types and point of contact for sample pull (who owns the data export?)
2) Procurement timeline for a small PO to cover the pilot (we'll send SOW + pricing)

I'll pull a one-page success-criteria doc and a draft SOW and share by EOD Monday. If this all looks right, can we target exec readout the week of Mar 1 for a go/no-go decision?

Thanks — Marcus

Marcus / Laura — attaching the runbook outline (paste below) and a short list of deliverables we'll provide during the pilot. Please review: 

Runbook highlights:
- Ingestion: we can accept pre-extracted JSON or PDFs. If PDFs are provided, we will include OCR as a pre-step (adds 1–2 days to setup).
- Scoring: we will provide a labelled test set (n=250 documents) and the scoring script. We recommend a first-pass acceptance threshold of F1 >= 0.86 for sandbox and >= 0.88 for pilot.
- Monitoring: daily accuracy snapshot, token usage dashboard, latency heatmap; alerts if median latency > 350ms.

Deliverables during pilot:
- Week 0: ingestion guide + sample mapping
- Weeks 1–2: labeled evaluation report (accuracy, error types)
- Weeks 3–6: business impact report + final exec deck (one slide per metric)
